dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: If two triangles have all three angles equal, can you conclude they are congruent?
dialogue_stages.student_response: I think so, because having all angles equal means they have the exact same shape.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Same shape means SIMILARITY, not CONGRUENCE! Imagine an equilateral triangle with side 1 cm, and another equilateral triangle with side 10 cm. Both have angles 60°, 60°, 60°, but one is 100 times larger in area than the other. They are definitely not congruent.

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: What is the minimum requirement involving sides to upgrade an angle-equality (AAA) condition into an authentic congruence proof?
dialogue_stages.student_response: You must establish that at least one pair of corresponding sides is equal in length. Then you can use ASA or AAS congruence.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Spot on! One corresponding side length fixes the scale factor k = 1, converting similarity into congruence.

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: If two right triangles have equal hypotenuses and one equal acute angle, are they congruent?
dialogue_stages.student_response: Yes! Both have a 90° angle, an equal acute angle, and equal hypotenuses. By AAS (or ASA by finding the third angle), they are congruent.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Perfect! AAS applies directly here. You demonstrated sharp discernment between valid congruence criteria and similarity traps.
